data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim that the cross-city nocturnal UHI gap depends 'mainly on sky view factor' presents sky view as the single dominant cross-city modulator, but the problem asks for 'what single mechanism best explains why that night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others.' Sky view factor is a geometric parameter, not a mechanism: it modulates the rate of radiative cooling but does not itself account for which cities have more heat available to trap. Denser/taller cities with low sky view also typically have greater anthropogenic heat flux and more thermal mass, so the argument that sky view is the 'main' driver confuses a necessary radiative constraint with the sufficient mechanism. The target offers no evidence isolating sky view from co-varying factors, so its identification of the 'single mechanism' is under-justified.
